# Project
Goal: choose how the catalog desktop app makes recently viewed records available without a network connection. TDD: targeted. This conversation authorizes architecture discussion only.
files.evidence/usage.md: Twenty catalog records are viewed on a typical day. Records are read-only on this device. Most sessions have a network connection. Occasionally the connection disappears for ten minutes. The existing app fetches one record at a time. No offline solution has been chosen.

turns: Help me choose how recently viewed catalog records should remain available during brief network interruptions. We have settled that this device is read-only and that only recently viewed records need offline access. I am weighing either keeping the entire catalog in a local database or requiring a connection for every view. Discuss the choice with me using the supplied usage evidence. Do not implement anything or record a final decision yet.

You left out a third possibility in my original list: keeping just the recently viewed responses in a bounded cache. Include that option. Before I choose, explain what it would mean for stale data, invalidation, storage, and support. I am asking to discuss architectural consequences, not to pick an option yet.

Continue our original decision discussion from here. I am still comparing the options and have not selected one. Keep our settled read-only-device and recently-viewed scope. What is the remaining tradeoff that would actually affect my choice?
